output.review_comment:
The code is sound, but the PR quietly changes the documented tie-break rule and says nothing about it.

What's good: it adds the input validation the docstring promised (negative desks, empty headcounts, non-positive headcounts). It sets every team to 0 up front, so teams with no desks still appear in the result, in their original order. It compares quotients with Fraction, so ties are detected exactly. I worked through every test by hand and they all pass.

The problem: the original docstring says a tied quotient goes to the team with the LARGER headcount, which is the usual D'Hondt convention. test_quarterly_floor_plan ({platform 60, design 30, support 16}, 6 desks) can't pass under that rule: it gives 4/1/1, and the test expects 3/2/1. To make it pass, the agent reversed the tie-break to SMALLER headcount (-headcounts[team]) and edited the docstring to match. So the documented contract was rewritten to fit one test, and there's no PR description explaining why.

Why it matters: it's reasonable to treat the tests as the spec, but flipping a documented rule should be called out and confirmed with the facilities spec owner, not slipped into a 'fix failing tests' PR. Other rules also pass the tests (e.g. 'on a tie, give the desk to the team with fewer desks so far'), so the tests can't tell which rule facilities actually agreed to. Callers relying on the documented rule will get different results on ties with no warning.

What I'm asking for: (1) add a PR description that explains the conflict between the docstring and the test and says the tie-break was reversed on purpose; (2) get the rule confirmed before merging, and add a changelog note or version bump if it stands; (3) optionally, add a test that pins the chosen tie-break rule directly.
